title: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
hookLine: he arrived in Medina with nothing, asked for the market, grew rich, and kept giving

cards: Here is an offer almost too generous to hear. A man has just arrived in Medina from Mecca with nothing.

His new brother, a man of the city named Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', says to him: I have more wealth than anyone among the helpers. Take half of it. And I have two wives; see which you like, and I'll divorce her so you can marry.
That is in Sahih al-Bukhari. Half of everything, offered to a man who has just arrived. The newcomer said no.
Gently. Today: the man who turned down half a fortune and asked for directions instead.

teach.b: His name was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, one of the emigrants. When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came to Medina, he paired emigrants with helpers as brothers, and Abd al-Rahman was paired with Sa'd.
His answer to the offer, in Bukhari's report: may God bless you in your family and your wealth.
Where is your market? Off he went.
He traded in cheese and butter and came back with a profit. Not long after, he turned up with traces of perfume on him and told the Prophet he had married. So the first thing to notice is dignity.

He received a huge kindness, blessed the giver, and kept his hands open for work. The biographies remember him becoming very wealthy, and giving, again and again, in large amounts for the community and its poor.
Tradition tells of whole caravans of goods given away; those accounts come from the sira, not from Bukhari, so hold them as stories the tradition tells.
And remember where we met him earlier on this road: a rich man, fasting, unable to eat his meal for remembering Mus'ab and his short cloak, afraid his reward had come early.
That is the second thing to notice. Wealth did not make him easy. It made him careful.

how: Muslims remember Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's reply, 'where is your market?', as a picture of earning with dignity; giving from what one earns, through zakat and voluntary charity, is part of Muslim practice.

s: Abd al-Rahman accepted half his brother's wealth
he blessed his brother and asked: where is your market?
the Prophet paired emigrants with helpers as brothers
that's how Abd al-Rahman came to be paired with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'.
the stories of his caravans given away are in Bukhari
those come from the sira, so they're held as stories the tradition tells.

games.q: you've just arrived in a new city with nothing. a new friend offers you half of everything he owns. what do you say?
o: bless him, and ask where the market is.
take a little, just to get started.
games.why: Abd al-Rahman said: may God bless you in your family and wealth. where is your market? and he went off to trade.

practice: Bring to mind something that went well lately, a paycheck, a good grade, a job finished, and let yourself enjoy it for a breath.
Then ask what part of it could go to someone else: a bit of money to someone in need, time if money is tight, or credit to the person who helped you get there.
If you pray, you can thank God for the success and ask that the giving be accepted.

wordCard.voice: Ibn Awf, the emigrant who turned down half a fortune, asked for the market instead, and grew rich while staying generous. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: servant of the Most Merciful, al-Rahman being one of God's names.

carryVoice: Your line: rich and giving. Earned with dignity, held with care. Day eight hundred forty, and a week of companions done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2048 / 3780 (brotherhood with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'; the offer; 'where is your market?'; cheese and butter; marriage)
